formNote: Mojidata IDS: ⿰礻豊. The Shuowen: 禮，履也。所以事神致福也 — “to tread: that by which one serves the spirits and brings blessing.” 豊 pictures a vessel full of offerings.
summary: Ritual and propriety: the forms of conduct, from sacrifice to greeting. The Shuowen glosses it as 履, “to tread”, a path walked; Confucius said that returning to ritual is humaneness.
placement: At the foot of the disk, below 仁: ritual as the ground the band runs on. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: What One Treads
satellites.evidence: The Shuowen glosses 禮 by sound with 履, “to tread, a shoe”: 所以事神致福也, “that by which one serves the spirits and brings blessing”. The vessel 豊 holds the offering.

satellites.title: The Sprout of Propriety
satellites.evidence: Mencius 2A6: 辭讓之心，禮之端也 — “the heart of declining and yielding is the sprout of propriety.” Ritual begins in the impulse to step aside for another.
